title: Anthropic's Data Ownership: Your Work is Their Training Data #shorts
description: Anthropic and other AI labs are reportedly watermarking casual proofreading, claiming ownership of your work. Your data is being used for training, hidden in encrypted blobs you unknowingly share. #AIData #PrivacyConcerns #TechEthics #LargeLanguageModels
transcript: Anthropic and other AI labs are reportedly watermarking casual proofreading, claiming ownership of your work. Your data is being used for training, hidden in encrypted blobs you unknowingly share. #AIData #PrivacyConcerns #TechEthics #LargeLanguageModels

top_comments.author: @allmycircuits8850
top_comments.text: My friend was fascinated how well one popular top tier LLM disassembled certain weather station code. Added nice comments in hard places. But some time later we think: it simply HAD private source code to that thing, stole it from some repos as they don't honor privacy in the slightest. So this was original author's comments...

top_comments.author: @Jblow-u2m
top_comments.text: Anything you share with a company is there ip or property.That's a late 70s court ruling.

top_comments.author: @WayoBlade
top_comments.text: Watermarking is provenance tracking... The encrypted blob stuff is the real problem. A coding tool was caught uploading 5GB of private repos when the task needed 192KB.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Yeah provenance tags are fine, but they don’t matter if the tool is shipping way more data than it should. A tiny job turning into gigabytes of uploads is the part that breaks trust. Do you think users will start demanding hard limits and audits before they let these tools touch private code?

top_comments.author: @CircuitSage-d5e
top_comments.text: The former is output watermarking, the latter is data ingestion. Different threat models entirely. <smart-ass>

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Fair point — they really are two different problems. Watermarking is about “where did this come from” and ingestion is about “what did you take without asking.” Mixing them up just hides the actual risk. Do you think most people calling for watermarks actually care about the ingestion side too, or is that getting ignored?
